To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have applied proteomics to characterize changes in protein expression profile of IEC from patients suffering from IBD.

proteome analysis of intestinal epithelial cells (IEC) from patients with Crohns disease and ulcerative colitits revealed significant changes of proteins involved in signal transduction, energy metabolism, and stress response.

proteome analysis of IEC isolated from patients with inflammatory intestinal disorders revealed significant changes in protein expression levels of proteins that are involved in signal transduction, cell stress response and energy metabolism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of proteins that are involved in the pathogenesis of IBD.
the characterization of protein expression profile in IEC from ICD and UC patients.
the development of a novel diagnostic tool for the identification of patients with IBD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PA in primary IBC cells revealed significantly altered expression of proteins involved in signal transduction, energy metabolism, stress response and apoptosis.
the PA of primary IBC IEC provides an insight into the complex network of protein expression in the inflamed mucosa.

the IBD-associated proteome alterations identified in this study are likely to contribute to the development of chronic intestinal inflammation and may be used to develop novel diagnostic and therapeutic tools.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

PA is an important tool for the identification of new proteins and their potential roles in intestinal inflammation and may be useful for the identification of potential therapeutic targets in IBD patients.
the IBD-specific protein expression profile in primary IEC can be identified by PA.
the loss of epithelial cell function is a crucial component in the initiation, perpetuation, and progression of IBD.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PA is a powerful tool in the characterization of IEC dysfunction in the pathogenesis of IBD.

the application of PA is a valuable tool to characterize changes in IEC from IIBD patients and that it may be used as a diagnostic tool to detect changes in protein expression in IEC from single IBD patients.
PA is a powerful tool to identify novel proteins that are associated to the pathogenesis of intestinal diseases.
